# Full binomial extrusion reserve and a shared simplex overlap constraint

This note first independently audits the supporting-facet extrusion
lemma, then proves a dimension-sensitive sharpening. It does not infer
that arbitrary scalar cap data are realizable by one convex body.

## 1. Independent audit of the source extrusion lemma

The argument in
`candidate b9b0fda52c8adffe`
is valid in its stated scope. If a facet F has one fixed normal height,
the section of D+F at any height is exactly D_t+F. The cap D is full
dimensional and proper, so every interior height section is full
(d-1)-dimensional; the two extreme heights have parameter measure zero.
Ordinary sectional BM, Fubini, and homothety by1/2 therefore give the
claimed factors and all binomial terms. A supporting face of zero
ambient volume is retained with its positive facet measure. The planar
formula is exact before the final containment in the middle cap.

The root note's planar mixed-area identity, residual midpoint inclusion,
reversal of the sorted cap order q_i=Q-U_i, and the necessary inequalities
in its Section5 also check independently. The statement F<a follows
already from k>b-a and k<a+b-2F. The stronger bound F<min(a,b) holds
if all three fibers are strictly nonheavy, but is not needed there.
The separate full-canonical-triangle proof correctly closes the planar
branch with only the B-nonheavy condition.

## 2. An elementary one-dimensional concave moment inequality

Let h be nonnegative and concave on an interval of length L>0,
positive on its interior. Fix integers m>=1 and 1<=p<=m. Put

    U=integral h(t)^m dt>0,
    c=[(m+1)U/L]^(1/m).

Then

    integral h(t)^p dt >= L c^p/(p+1)
      =[(m+1)^(p/m)/(p+1)] L^(1-p/m) U^(p/m).           (1)

Here is a proof without assuming a moment comparison theorem. Let
H=max h and let ell(s) be the length of the strict superlevel set
{t:h(t)>s}. For 0<=s<H these sets are intervals. Concavity of h and
one-dimensional addition of intervals show that ell is concave on
[0,H); moreover ell(0)=L. The superlevel chord implies
ell(s)>=L(1-s/H) on that interval, by first comparing with any level
below H and then taking its limit. Layer cake consequently gives

    U=m integral_0^H s^(m-1)ell(s) ds >= L H^m/(m+1),

so H<=c. Compare ell, extended by zero above H, with
ell_0(s)=L(1-s/c)_+. On [0,H), the difference g=ell-ell_0 is concave
and has g(0)=0. Therefore g(s)/s is nonincreasing for s>0. Above H the
difference is nonpositive. Thus g has at most one sign change, from
nonnegative to nonpositive. This argument allows a terminal downward
jump of ell when h has a positive-length plateau at its maximum.

Layer cake and the definition of c give
integral s^(m-1)g(s) ds=0. If p<m, choose a crossing level s0 and
multiply this identity by s0^(p-m). The function s^(p-m) is decreasing,
so pointwise

    s^(m-1)g(s)[s^(p-m)-s0^(p-m)]>=0.

Integrating proves integral s^(p-1)g(s) ds>=0. Cases in which g is
identically zero, or has only one sign, follow immediately from its
zero m-moment. Integrals at zero are finite by boundedness and p>=1.
A final layer-cake integration proves(1); p=m is equality by definition.
For a nondegenerate tent h whose two sides are affine and vanish at
the interval endpoints, ell(s)=L(1-s/H), so equality holds for every p.
The one-sided affine cone h(t)=H(1-t/L) also gives equality.

## 3. Sharp full-binomial supporting-facet reserve

Let d>=2, m=d-1. Let D be a full-dimensional convex body, and let F
be a full (d-1)-dimensional convex body in a hyperplane perpendicular
to a unit vector e. Define

    U=|D|,   f=H_(d-1)(F),
    L=max_D e.x-min_D e.x,   P=fL,
    r=(dU/P)^(1/(d-1)).

The section-root h(t)=|D_t|^(1/m) is concave by ordinary sectional BM.
The exact height-slice identity and (1), applied term by term to the
binomial expansion, give

    |D+F| >= U+P
       +sum_(j=1)^(d-2) binom(d-1,j)
             [d^((d-1-j)/(d-1))/(d-j)]
             U^((d-1-j)/(d-1)) P^(j/(d-1))
      = P J_d(r),                                      (2)

where

    J_d(r)=integral_0^1(1+rt)^(d-1)dt
           =[(1+r)^d-1]/(d r).

To check the coefficients, the term with section power p=d-1-j has
integral lower bound L(dU/L)^(p/(d-1))/(p+1); multiplication by
f^(j/(d-1)) gives precisely P(dU/P)^(p/(d-1))/(p+1).
The endpoint terms p=0 and p=d-1 are exactly P and U. Thus no
binomial term or dimensional homothety factor is suppressed.

This inequality is sharp as a standalone facet-extrusion statement.
Take D to be a cone with horizontal sections t r F, 0<=t<=1, using
height interval length L. Sectional BM is equality, the section root
is affine, U=P r^(d-1)/d, and every moment inequality is equality.
The statement does not say that several cap cones belonging to a
single A simultaneously attain equality.

In particular

    d=2: |D+F|=U+P,
    d=3: |D+F|>=U+P+sqrt(3UP),                         (3)
    d=4: |D+F|>=U+P+(3/2)4^(1/3)U^(1/3)P^(2/3)
                         +4^(2/3)U^(2/3)P^(1/3).

## 4. Application to actual simplex-facet caps

Let B={x:v_i.x<=1, i=1,...,d+1} be a full-dimensional simplex with
sum_i v_i=0, and let b=|B|. Let A,K be full-dimensional convex bodies
with (A+B)/2 contained in K. Consider the d+1 ambient caps

    H_i={(z,x):v_i.x>=z}

at bases -1,0,1. Assume all A cuts are proper, and put

    U_i=|A intersect {v_i.x>=-1}|,
    q_i=|K intersect {v_i.x>=0}|,
    h_i=max_A v_i.x,
    P_i=[d b/(d+1)](h_i+1).

Every B restriction is its FULL facet. Its facet measure divided by
||v_i|| is d b/(d+1). To verify this, the barycentric affine coordinates
of this simplex are (1-v_i.x)/(d+1): they sum to one, vanish on the
corresponding facets, and take value one at the opposite vertex.
Thus zero is the centroid. The d+1 pyramids joining zero to the facets
have equal volume b/(d+1); the pyramid formula proves the stated facet
measure identity. Properness gives h_i+1>0.

Applying (2) to each actual captured A cap and its actual B facet gives

    2^d q_i >= P_i J_d((dU_i/P_i)^(1/(d-1))).           (4)

If these caps share actual mass Q, then q_i=Q-U_i and

    2^d Q >= 2^d U_i
                 +P_i J_d((dU_i/P_i)^(1/(d-1))).       (5)

For d=3 this becomes the explicit necessary inequality

    8Q >=9U_i+P_i+sqrt(3U_i P_i).                      (6)

All quantities refer to one A, one K, and the same B. The inequalities
need no criticality beyond identifying the common mass Q; if critical
section conditions are also used, they are additional constraints.

## 5. A dimension-aware shared two-residual overlap

Let Gamma=Gamma_d and k=|K|, a=|A|. For d>=2 put

    kappa=1/Gamma-2 in (0,1).

Order U_1<=...<=U_(d+1). The ordinary distal cap-cover profile, using
its top-three consequence, gives

    k <= Q/Gamma-F,   F=U_1+U_2+kappa U_3.             (7)

For clarity, the top-three consequence follows by setting the profile
threshold to the third largest cap mass: the sum above that threshold
contains the largest two, while its coefficient at that threshold is
1/Gamma-2=kappa. The middle caps cover because sum_i v_i=0. This is
the already proved ordinary profile, not a new assumed inequality.

If Q<=Gamma(a+b+k)/2 and b<=a+k, equations(7) give

    k<=a+b-2F,   F<=a,   Q<=Gamma(a+b-F).              (8)

The two strict residuals of A associated with U_1,U_2 then overlap in
volume at least a-U_1-U_2>=kappa U_3>0. At a point in that actual
intersection, v_1.x and v_2.x are both below-1. Hence

    sum_(i=3)^(d+1) v_i.x>2,
    sum_(i=3)^(d+1)(h_i+1)>d+1,
    sum_(i=3)^(d+1)P_i>d b.                            (9)

This retains the shared point of the two actual residuals. It is
stronger than separately asserting that some cap has a large height.
In dimension three, combine(6) and(9) to obtain

    16Q>9(U_3+U_4)+3b
                    +sqrt(3U_3 P_3)+sqrt(3U_4 P_4).    (10)

The direction of the strict inequality follows by summing(6) and using
P_3+P_4>3b. The individual P_i in the root terms remain the actual
shared-body heights; they may not be independently optimized and then
claimed realizable. The planar proof is recovered from the single
remaining direction, but (10) by itself is not claimed to close d=3.

## 6. Simultaneous support-incidence and first-moment charges

Write m=d+1 and H_i=h_i+1, so P_i=(db/m)H_i. For an interior point
x of A let I(x)={i:v_i.x>=-1}. The missing coordinates satisfy
v_i.x+1<0, while sum_i(v_i.x+1)=m. Hence

    sum_(i in I(x))(v_i.x+1)>=m,
    sum_(i in I(x))H_i>m.                              (11)

The last inequality is strict because x is interior and every v_i is
nonzero. Thus a membership pattern I can occur on positive A volume
only if sum_(i in I)P_i>db. Integrating(11) gives

    sum_i P_i U_i>db a.                                (12)

There is a stronger moment version. Define the actual residual first
moments in their coordinate heights,

    R_i=integral_(A intersect {v_i.x<-1})(-1-v_i.x) dx,
    R=sum_i R_i>0.

Properness makes every R_i positive. The pointwise positive/negative
part identity yields exactly

    sum_i integral_(A_i)(v_i.x+1) dx=m a+R.             (13)

For any convex body D whose coordinate g has range[0,H], its mean
coordinate is at most dH/(d+1). Indeed, homothety of D about a point at
its minimum maps it into {g<=s} with volume(s/H)^d|D|. Integrating the
complementary tail gives integral_D g<=dH|D|/(d+1). Apply this to each
proper captured cap A_i and combine with(13):

    sum_i H_i U_i >=(m/d)(m a+R),
    sum_i P_i U_i >=m b a+bR>m b a.                    (14)

This retains actual residual first moments, which cannot be prescribed
independently of the common body A. No simultaneous cone equality is
assumed. In particular (14) is stronger than the pure incidence bound.

## 7. A cap-to-residual density bound and a further moment constraint

The residual first moments in(14) have an explicit lower bound from
the captured support and volume. For one cap, put g=v_i.x+1, H=H_i,
U=U_i, t=U/a in(0,1), and let rho(s) be the coordinate density of A
at g=s. Thus integral rho=a; the Euclidean section density includes
the factor1/||v_i||. Its(d-1)-root is concave on the support interval.

Let rho_0 be the density at the proper cut g=0. The straight cone
from that section to a highest support point at g=H lies inside the
captured cap. Therefore

    U>=rho_0 H/d.

For a residual height -s<0, concavity of the section root, compared
with its values at0 and the nonnegative limiting value at H, gives

    rho(-s) <=rho_0(1+s/H)^(d-1)
             <=(dU/H)(1+s/H)^(d-1).                   (15)

This bound is understood as zero outside the actual support, where
it remains valid. Measurability and endpoint limits follow from the
usual interior section continuity for a convex body.

Among all nonnegative densities bounded by the right side of(15) and
having mass a-U on s>=0, the first moment is minimized by filling that
upper bound from zero to a cutoff L. To prove this, let e(s) denote
the increasing upper bound, choose L with integral_0^L e=a-U, and
subtract e1_[0,L] from the given density. The difference has integral
zero, is nonpositive below L and nonnegative above L. Multiplication
by s-L and integration proves the first-moment comparison. The cutoff
is L=H(t^(-1/d)-1), so direct integration gives

    R_i >=H_i a[(d/m)t_i^(-1/d)-1+t_i/m],
    t_i=U_i/a.                                         (16)

For completeness, substitute w=1+s/H in the integral of s e(s): it
is dUH[w^(d+1)/(d+1)-w^d/d]_1^(t^(-1/d)), exactly the displayed
expression. Combining(13), the captured centroid bound, and(16)
proves the simultaneous actual-body inequality

    sum_i H_i G_d(t_i)>=m,
    G_d(t)=1+[(d-1)/(d+1)]t-[d/(d+1)]t^(-1/d).          (17)

Neither (16) nor (17) says that the captured centroid and backward
density estimates are jointly sharp. They generally have different
cone equality cases. They are valid inequalities for the same actual
caps, which suffices for their use as necessary conditions.

## 8. The global simplex coefficient gives a matching binomial bound

Use the standard mixed-volume normalization

    |B+sA|=sum_(j=0)^d binom(d,j) X_j s^j,
    X_j=V(A[j],B[d-j]), X_0=b, X_d=a.

The first variation at the facets of B is

    d X_1=sum_i [facet_area_i/||v_i||] h_i
           =sum_i P_i-db.                              (18)

This is the ordinary support-function first variation of polytope
volume. It follows directly by summing the facet strips; face
intersections of codimension at least two contribute O(s^2).
One can translate A to contain zero to make the one-sided strip
argument literal; the coefficient is invariant under translation
because the facet-area-weighted normals of B balance. General A
follow by Hausdorff polygonal/polyhedral approximation and continuity
of mixed volumes.

Classical Alexandrov--Fenchel says X_j^2>=X_(j-1)X_(j+1), so the
logarithms are concave. With r=(a/X_1)^(1/(d-1)), interpolation between
indices1 and d gives X_j>=X_1 r^(j-1) for1<=j<=d. Hence actual midpoint
compatibility gives

    2^d k >= |A+B|
       >=b+X_1[(1+r)^d-1]/r.                          (19)

Only standard Alexandrov--Fenchel is used here; its consequence is
proved by the displayed finite log-concavity interpolation. All
bodies have positive volume, so X_1 and r are positive. Equations(2)
and(19) have the same binomial polynomial, but the former uses each
actual cap and facet, while the latter couples their global support
sum through one actual A.

For d=3, put X=sum_i P_i-3b=3X_1. Then(19) reads

    8k>=a+b+X+sqrt(3aX)
       =a+sum_i P_i-2b+sqrt(3a(sum_i P_i-3b)).           (20)

This bound cannot be discarded while optimizing the P_i separately.
It does not by itself assert that passing scalar data arise from any
common convex body.

## 9. Exact obstruction to closing with these scalar consequences alone

The preceding inequalities are concrete necessary conditions. They do
not yet close the d=3 branch: the following EXACT formal data pass all
of them while their common mass lies below the desired target. This
is a certificate of insufficiency of the listed scalar tests only.
There is NO claim that these data are realized by a convex body, that
the caps are critical, or that OC is false.

Normalize b=1 and take

    a=1/80,   k=99/100,   Q=4223/10000,
    t=( (2/5)^3, (3/4)^3, (7/8)^3, (8/9)^3 ),
    U_i=a t_i,  q_i=Q-U_i,
    P=(3/10,309/100,601/200,601/200),   H_i=4P_i/3.

All U_i are strictly between zero and a and in increasing order.
With Gamma=27/64 and kappa=10/27, direct rational arithmetic gives

    Gamma(a+b+k)/2-Q=131/1280000>0,
    2max(a,b,k)<a+b+k,
    k<=Q/Gamma-(U_1+U_2+kappa U_3),
    a<=U_4+U_3+kappa U_2.

The formal data pass the complete local binomial bound because each
8Q-9U_i-P_i is positive and its square exceeds 3U_iP_i. They pass
P_3+P_4>3b and sum_i P_iU_i>4ba. Since t_i are rational cubes,
G_3(t_i) is rational, and their residual-moment surplus is exactly

    sum_i H_i G_3(t_i)-4
       =9393445081/19595520000>0.

Their global first mixed coefficient is X=sum_iP_i-3b=32/5. The
nonradical side of the global AF test is

    8k-a-b-X=203/400>0,
    (203/400)^2-3aX=2809/160000>0.

They also satisfy the usual first mixed-volume lower bound
(X/3)^3>=a, as well as sum_(j!=i)P_j>3 for each proper residual.

Even the exact membership-pattern obstruction can be respected by a
nonnegative ABSTRACT incidence measure. Put w=2a-sum_iU_i>0, set
mass w on pattern{4}, mass U_1 on{1,4}, and put

    d2=U_2, d3=U_3, d4=U_4-w-U_1,
    mass{2,3}=(d2+d3-d4)/2,
    mass{2,4}=(d2+d4-d3)/2,
    mass{3,4}=(d3+d4-d2)/2.

All five masses are positive; they sum to a and their cap marginals
are exactly U_i. Every used pattern I satisfies sum_(i in I)P_i>3.
This construction certifies only the abstract incidence conditions;
it does not supply points having these masses in one uniform convex A.
That distinction is essential.

The exact verifier is
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_supporting_facet_binomial_reserve_slab_recovery.py`.
Its Fraction-only checks verify the binomial cone identities, elementary
concave-moment examples, and this formal insufficiency certificate.
Numerical screens were used only to locate candidates; the claims in
this section are the exact rational identities and inequalities above.
Thus the new geometric reserves are proved, but the higher-dimensional
full-simplex critical branch still needs a further actual-body argument.
